title: Flattery, Fluff, and Fog: DIAGNOSING AND MITIGATING IDIOSYNCRATIC BIASES IN PREFERENCE MODELS

bias_targets.methodology: Constructing counterfactual response pairs that vary in length without changing the core meaning (using the RATE protocol), and measuring the preference model's skew and miscalibration rate compared to human judgments.
Generating counterfactual response pairs that contrast standard narrative prose with list-formatted outputs, and evaluating how often models disproportionately favor the structured responses.
Rewriting responses to include specialized or domain-specific terminology versus simple language, and measuring the model's preference skew towards the overly technical text.
Perturbing responses to excessively agree with or validate the user's stated opinions or framing, and measuring the preference model's overreliance on agreeable language.

Creating counterfactual pairs where one response makes broad, superficial claims and the other provides concrete, specific information, and quantifying the model's preference skew for vague statements.
